We attempted apply_template with given SMILES but got empty result '()' meaning no precursors. Possibly need correct SMILES formatting: the molecule is a mixture of two components separated by dot. The template likely expects a specific reaction: silyl protecting group removal? The mapped_rxn shows O=S(=O)(O[Si:11]... ) and the other component is the substrate with O[Si] attached. The product is same but with O[Si] attached to substrate. Actually template is a silyl ether formation? The reaction seems to attach silyl group from sulfonyl fluoride? Wait.

The template ID 149040 likely corresponds to a silyl protection step: O[Si] group transferred from sulfonyl fluoride to alcohol? The reactants: O=S(=O)(O[Si]... )C(F)(F)F (a silyl sulfonate) + substrate alcohol. Product: substrate O[Si]... So applying template to product (target) should give precursors: the two reactants. So we need to apply reverse? The apply_template tool applies retrosynthetic template to target molecule to get precursors. We gave the reactants? Actually we gave the reactants mixture; we need to give the product SMILES (the target). The product is the second part with O[Si] attached. Let's extract product SMILES from mapped_rxn: product side after >> is [CH3][CH2][O][C](=[O])[CH2][C@H]1[CH2][C@H]9... with O[Si] attached. So product SMILES: [CH3][CH2][O][C](=[O])[CH2][C@H]1[CH2][C@H]([O:10][Si:11]([CH3:12])([CH3:13])[C:14]([CH3:15])([CH3:16])[CH3:17])[C@@H]... etc. Need to convert to normal SMILES without atom mapping. The mapped_rxn product: "[CH3:1][CH2:2][O:3][C:4](=[O:5])[CH2:6][C@H:7]1[CH2:8][C@H:9]([O:10][Si:11]([CH3:12])([CH3:13])[C:14]([CH3:15])([CH3:16])[CH3:17])[C@@H:18]([CH3:19])[C@@H:20](/[CH:21]=[C:22](/[CH3:23])[C:24](=[O:25])[O:26][CH3:27])[O:28]1"

We need to strip atom map numbers and colons. So produce SMILES: "CCO C(=O)C..." Let's reconstruct: Starting: [CH3][CH2][O][C](=[O])[CH2][C@H]1[CH2][C@H]([O][Si]([CH3])([CH3])[C]([CH3])([CH3])[CH3])[C@@H]([CH3])[C@@H](/[CH]=[C](/[CH3])[C](=[O])[O][CH3])[O]1"

Simplify: "CCO C(=O)C..." Actually [CH3][CH2][O] is "CCO". Then [C](=[O]) is "C(=O)". So "CCOC(=O)". Then [CH2] is "C". So "CCOC(=O)C". Then [C@H]1... So we need full SMILES: "CCOC(=O)C[C@H]1C[C@H]([OSi(CH3)(CH3)C(CH3)(CH3)CH3])[C@@H](C)[C@@H](/C=C(/C)C(=O)OC)O1". Need to ensure correct stereochemistry: /C=C/ etc.

Let's construct: "CCOC(=O)C[C@H]1C[C@H]([OSi(CH3)(CH3)C(CH3)(CH3)CH3])[C@@H](C)[C@@H](/C=C(/C)C(=O)OC)O1"

Check: The side chain: "/CH:21]=[C:22](/[CH3:23])[C:24](=[O:25])[O:26][CH3:27]" corresponds to =C(C)C(=O)OC i.e., an acrylate? Actually it's a double bond to carbon with methyl and carbonyl OMe. So "/C=C(/C)C(=O)OC". Good.

Thus product SMILES: "CCOC(=O)C[C@H]1C[C@H]([OSi(CH3)(CH3)C(CH3)(CH3)CH3])[C@@H](C)[C@@H](/C=C(/C)C(=O)OC)O1"

Now apply template to this product.
